newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares slide below 1,400 in sharp correction.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares slide below 1,400 in sharp correction.

text.p: Greek equities which started the session in an upbeat mood saw the early drift turn into a sharp correction with the index falling below the 1,400 support level to settle 1.83 percent lower.
Market watchers saw no correlation with weakness in other Euro bourses following Wall Street's sharp fall last Friday.

"The market was up almost half a percentage point before it started to drift lower. Then, suddenly, it started to slide sharply. Rumours of disappointing first quarter results of National Mortgage Bank pulled banks lower," said a fund manager.

"I don't think there was any impact from other European bourses. It would have been obvious from the opening which was firm in Athens. I don't think there is much more on the downside -- 1,370 should be strong support," he said.
Based on Friday's close Greek stocks have gained 52.2 percent since the beginning of the year and were closing in on this year's high of 1,454.83 points.
Following a better-than-expected March CPI inflation figure -- 6.0 percent -- banks started a new round of interest rate cuts last week.

And late in the session the Bank of Greece said Greece's current account deficit rose 59 percent year-on-year to $4.5 billion in 1996, the widening reflecting a 7.1 percent higher trade deficit of $18.3 billion.

"From a technical perspective, the 1,450 level appeared to be a resistance level for the market. The index is consolidating and facing support at 1,401 and 1,352 points -- the latter looking more improbable," said Omega Securities.

On Friday, the Public Petroleum Corporation (DEP) announced it had picked Salomon Brothers, SBC Warburg, Ionian Finance and Ernst & Young as advisors for a planned 10 percent flotation on the Athens bourse this year and the group's restructuring.
Meanwhile, subscriptions to Xiosbank's IPO start on Tuesday April 15-18. The bank is going public at 2,650 drachmas a share seeking to raise 4.43 billion.
The Athens general share index settled 1.83 percent or 26.05 points lower at 1,394.98 from Friday's 1,421.03 close, after opening at 1,427.34. The session's low was at 1,386.24 points.
Turnover was 13.8 billion drachmas on volume of 3.4 million shares. Decliners led advancers 174 to 56 with 17 issues unchanged on 247 traded.
Banks fell 2.25 percent with construction also down 2.02 percent. Industrials ended 1.31 percent weaker.
